related_questions.question: What do US citizens need to enter France?

text_blocks.snippet: U.S. citizens can enter France for up to 90 days without a visa, provided they have a valid U.S. passport. The passport must be valid for at least three months beyond your intended departure date from the Schengen area, according to the U.S. Embassy and Consulates in France. While a visa isn't required for short stays, travelers may need to show proof of onward or return travel, sufficient funds, and accommodation details. Starting in late 2024, U.S. citizens will also need to obtain an ETIAS (European Travel Information and Authorization System) authorization before traveling to France and other Schengen countries, according to ivisatravel.com.
